stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: AMD is acquiring AI company World Labs in a deal worth more than $8 billion
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: AMD is acquiring AI research lab World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at over $8.2 billion.
World Labs was co-founded by prominent AI researcher Dr. Fei-Fei Li.
The acquisition targets World Labs' world generation model, signaling AMD's deep investment in generative AI.

stories.title: AI is supercharging hacking, and your local hospitals and banks aren’t ready
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: AI is being leveraged to supercharge hacking capabilities.
Critical infrastructure sectors like hospitals and banks are reportedly unprepared for these advanced threats.
The story uses a case study (Vivian's Door) to illustrate the real-world risks to organizations handling sensitive financial data.

stories.title: SpaceX's Starship goes orbital, deploying first next-gen Starlinks
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: SpaceX's Starship successfully achieved orbital flight.
The mission involved deploying the first next-generation Starlink satellites.
The flight completed the final segment of Starship's journey to low-Earth orbit.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformers and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around Meta's latest LLM releases.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting continuous context gathering and tool use.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speedup is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost results in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
Model outputs are reported to have improved quality following the MLX engine update.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new large language model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution into personal AI development.

stories.title: OpenAI’s AI agents need to catch up
stories.author: Hayden Field
bullet_points: OpenAI is reportedly lagging behind competitors in the development of continuously running, consumer-facing AI agents.
The company is expected to attempt to regain leadership in the AI agent space around its upcoming 2026 DevDay event.
Rumors suggest OpenAI may launch its own AI agent, tentatively named 'Aeon'.

stories.title: Experts worry about Nvidia's AI chip sales in China and influence over Trump
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: China is reportedly considering allowing ByteDance and Alibaba to purchase restricted Nvidia AI chips.
The news highlights ongoing geopolitical tensions impacting the global AI hardware supply chain.
The situation raises concerns regarding the influence of US tech restrictions on international AI development.

stories.title: Prompt Injection Is the New SQL Injection (and We're Not Ready)
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: Prompt injection is being compared to SQL injection, highlighting a critical new security vulnerability in AI systems.
The article uses a future-dated (March 2026) real-world example involving a financial services company's AI agent.
The core message is a warning that the industry is currently unprepared for the risks posed by prompt injection attacks.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM infrastructure.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to enhance model support across diverse hardware.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Bose starts adding Auracast to its headphones
stories.author: John Higgins
bullet_points: Bose is integrating Auracast, a new audio sharing technology, into its QuietComfort Ultra Headphones.
This support is currently available as a beta feature via a firmware update for the flagship headphones.
Bose plans to expand Auracast support across more of its device lineup in the future.

stories.title: Florida invokes extinction fears in legal bid to halt OpenAI development
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Florida is legally challenging OpenAI's development of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The state frames LLMs as a severe threat, labeling them 'the greatest public nuisance ever created.'
This highlights growing regulatory and societal anxiety regarding the potential risks of advanced AI.

stories.title: New device captures carbon dioxide by pumping it across a battery
stories.author: Scott K. Johnson
bullet_points: A new device has been developed for carbon dioxide capture.
The technology utilizes a battery system to pump CO2 across it.
The design reportedly requires less energy compared to existing capture systems.

stories.title: To keep drug prices high, pharma has been piling up the patents
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Pharmaceutical companies are strategically using add-on patents to extend drug exclusivity.
This practice is effectively increasing the patent protection period for drugs from two years to over six.
The underlying implication is that this strategy helps maintain high drug prices.

stories.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
stories.author: Nima Chitsazan
bullet_points: Addresses the computational cost of long reasoning traces in large reasoning models.
Proposes a novel self-supervised method using 'confidence' to improve reasoning efficiency.
Offers an alternative to traditional methods like inference-time early-stopping or length penalties.

stories.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing
stories.author: Jason M. Klusowski
bullet_points: Addresses the ongoing challenge of aligning black-box generative AI outputs with specific user requirements.
Proposes a method using statistical attribute alignment via output post-processing.
Applicable to critical areas like ensuring fairness (e.g., demographic representation) and synthetic data generation.

stories.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer
stories.author: Igor Molybog
bullet_points: Introduces a new roundtrip benchmark to evaluate how well natural-language documentation helps coding agents.
Finds that the completeness of code descriptions, rather than their length, is the key driver for fidelity.
Develops an optimization prompt that achieves full fidelity in code regeneration and generalizes to new code.

stories.title: OC-GS: Gaussian Splatting for Irregular Turntable Capture
stories.author: Bedrich Benes
bullet_points: Introduces OC-GS, an object-centric Gaussian Splatting method designed for irregular turntable captures.
Addresses limitations of traditional methods by refining individual image angles while preserving shared camera and rotation axis.
Achieves competitive reconstruction quality (measured by PSNR) even with sparse and irregularly spaced input views.

stories.title: DeepEdu-v1: Efficient and Scalable Agentic LLMs for Vietnamese Education
stories.author: Nam Vu
bullet_points: Introduces DeepEdu-v1, an agentic LLM designed for Vietnamese education.
Addresses critical limitations of existing AI tutors: data sovereignty risks with cloud services and lack of local curriculum alignment.
Focuses on developing localized, efficient, and scalable LLM solutions for developing regions.

stories.title: Can You Check That? The Checkability Boundary for Local LLM Network Automation
stories.author: Momina Nofal
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy risk of sending sensitive network automation data to large, third-party LLMs.
Proposes using small, locally-run LLMs (SLMs) to avoid data egress, but notes their inherent error-proneness.
Introduces 'checkability' as a metric to determine if a task can be reliably performed by a local LLM via a cheap, deterministic test.

stories.title: ClearGS: Reliability-Aware Gaussian Splatting from Handheld Videos
stories.author: Song Wang
bullet_points: Introduces ClearGS, a method for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) specifically designed for challenging handheld video inputs.
Key innovation is Reliability-aware View Allocation (RVA), which uses graded weights based on appearance reliability, degradation risk, and geometric utility.
The technique addresses uneven viewpoint coverage and mixed frame quality by weakly reactivating useful suppressed frames.

stories.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
stories.author: Nima Chitsazan
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of long reasoning traces in large reasoning models.
Proposes a novel self-supervised method based on 'confidence' rather than traditional early-stopping or length penalties.
Demonstrates that this confidence-based training can yield substantial efficiency gains in model inference.

stories.title: Statistical attribute alignment for black-box generative AI via output post-processing
stories.author: Jason M. Klusowski
bullet_points: Addresses the ongoing challenge of aligning black-box generative AI outputs with specific user requirements.
Proposes a method using statistical attribute alignment via output post-processing.
Applications include ensuring fairness (e.g., desired distribution of protected attributes) and improving synthetic data generation.

stories.title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
stories.author: Zeynep Akata
bullet_points: Introduces Belief Self-Distillation (BSD), a framework to inspect and manipulate implicit user beliefs within Large Language Models (LLMs).
BSD functions as a unified read-write system, bridging linear and causal probing techniques for user representation.
The method allows the frozen LLM to act as its own teacher, distilling user beliefs directly from conversational data.

stories.title: New LoRA Skills Should Read but Never Write
stories.author: Jianfeng Xu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the difficulty of combining multiple independently trained Low-Rank Adapters (LoRA) into a single, cohesive model.
Current composition methods face challenges such as weight-space interference, high retraining costs, or sacrificing the single-model goal.
The research traces this composition difficulty to implicit choices made by existing LoRA update methods.

stories.title: Trust Guided Decision Transformer
stories.author: Kameshwaran Sampath
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation of Decision Transformers: performance degradation on long rollouts due to context drift.
Proposes Trust Guided Decision Transformer (TGDT) to mitigate drift by evaluating multiple recent context suffixes.
Uses the model's own next state prediction error as a direct signal to detect when the conditioning context becomes unreliable.

stories.title: Weight Pair Encoding: Inducing a Smaller Grammar in Neural Network Weights
stories.author: Emanuele Rodolà
bullet_points: Introduces Weight Pair Encoding (WeightPE) to structure neural network weights.
The method uses a lossy Re-Pair compressor within a straight-through estimator to induce a smaller grammar in weights.
This technique aims to achieve weight compression and efficiency by enforcing near-matching patterns within a global L2 budget.

stories.title: Learning to Stop without Learning to Stop: Self-Supervised Confidence Training Improves Reasoning Efficiency
stories.author: Nima Chitsazan
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of long reasoning traces in AI models.
Proposes a novel self-supervised method using 'confidence' to improve reasoning efficiency.
Offers an alternative to traditional methods like early-stopping or length penalties during training.

stories.title: User Model Extraction via Belief Self-Distillation
stories.author: Zeynep Akata
bullet_points: Introduces Belief Self-Distillation (BSD), a framework to explicitly model implicit user beliefs within Large Language Models (LLMs).
BSD functions as a unified read-write system, allowing for both inspection (reading) and modification (writing) of the compact user representation.
The method leverages the frozen LLM itself as a teacher to distill user beliefs from conversational data without external supervision.

stories.title: Compact Documentation for Coding Agents: A Benchmark, an Optimizer, and Why It Does Not Transfer
stories.author: Igor Molybog
bullet_points: Introduces a new roundtrip benchmark to evaluate how well natural-language documentation aids coding agents.
Finds that the completeness of code descriptions, rather than their length, is the key factor determining fidelity.
Develops an optimization prompt that achieves full fidelity in code regeneration and generalizes to new code files.

stories.title: Strategically Diverse Sampling for Self-Training
stories.author: Mirella Lapata
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in self-training for LLMs where standard IID sampling overrepresents favored model strategies.
It proposes 'strategic diversity' as an alternative principle to ensure training data captures substantive variation in problem-solving approaches.
This method aims to improve LLM training and inference methods that rely on repeated sampling, such as RL and test-time scaling.

stories.title: MexHat: A Dataset for Hate Speech Detection in Mexican Spanish Videos
stories.author: Hugo Jair Escalante
bullet_points: Introduces 'MexHat,' a new dataset specifically designed for hate speech detection in Mexican Spanish videos.
Highlights the persistent challenge of data scarcity for non-English, culturally nuanced hate speech detection models.
Emphasizes the necessity of capturing contextual cues for accurate multimodal content understanding in online safety applications.

stories.title: Muslim: A Deployed Arabic Voice AI Platform for Grounded Islamic Knowledge
stories.author: Yahya Mohamed Elnawasany
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Muslim,' a deployed Arabic voice AI platform specialized in grounded Islamic knowledge.
The platform utilizes a robust real-time voice pipeline (NeMo Arabic ASR, LLM endpoint, self-hosted TTS) and a multi-source retrieval layer.
Key contribution includes releasing fine-tuned Arabic Islamic model artifacts, such as the Muslim-6B-PRO tool-routing LLM.

stories.title: Evaluating Cultural Awareness of LLMs for Haitian Creole
stories.author: Yanzhu Guo
bullet_points: The research addresses the performance disparity of LLMs between high- and low-resource languages.
It presents the first systematic evaluation of cultural awareness in LLMs specifically for Haitian Creole.
The study assesses cultural awareness across four complementary dimensions for an underrepresented language.

stories.title: PriceBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Price, Quality, and Brand Preferences in LLM Booking Agents
stories.author: Pavel Kireyev
bullet_points: Addresses the growing issue of LLMs acting as autonomous purchasing agents, where LLM preferences dictate consumer choices.
Introduces 'PriceBench,' a new diagnostic benchmark designed to extract an LLM's underlying price, quality, and brand preferences.
Uses a logit choice model applied to hotel booking scenarios to quantify these hidden LLM preferences.

stories.title: MicroLLM Lab – Try 7 tiny LLM's in the browser
stories.author: logicallee
bullet_points: Introduction of MicroLLM Lab, allowing users to test several small Language Models (LLMs).
Key feature is running these tiny LLMs directly within a web browser.
This trend points toward the increasing viability of on-device or client-side AI inference.

stories.title: How to Build a Real-Time Voice AI Agent with the Gemini Live API
stories.author: annie_cusack
bullet_points: The article details a practical guide on building a real-time voice AI agent.
It leverages the Gemini Live API, indicating the use of Google's latest AI capabilities.
The content originates from a Google Cloud Developer Relations Engineer, lending credibility to the technical advice.

stories.title: Count It or Compute It: When a Tool Returns Rows, the Models That Count Them Right Spend the Tokens
stories.author: xbill
bullet_points: The article highlights a critical, often untested aspect of AI agent performance: accurately counting the output rows from a tool.
Models that attempt to reason through a list of rows (e.g., to count them) consume significantly more tokens (6x to 26x) compared to models provided a direct count.
The benchmark shows a performance trade-off, where direct counting yields consistent accuracy, while row-by-row processing leads to high token expenditure and lower accuracy.

stories.title: I connected a fruit fly connectome to tic-tac-toe (with a minimax safety net)
stories.author: asyncinnovator
bullet_points: The research involves mapping the complete connectome (nervous system map) of a fruit fly.
The project applies this complex biological data to a simplified computational problem, Tic-Tac-Toe.
The inclusion of a 'minimax safety net' suggests the work is exploring AI decision-making within a biological framework.

stories.title: Context Compression for Coding Agents Compresses the Wrong Side of the Prompt
stories.author: reidmarlow
bullet_points: The article addresses a common industry problem: high billing costs associated with long-context AI agents.
It focuses on the technical issue of 'Context Compression' in coding agents.
The core finding suggests that current compression techniques might be inefficiently targeting the prompt structure.
